xfail.reason: end displacement 2.777e-3 vs 4.200e-3 from the sum of uniaxial-stress material points at F = 1.1e-3: the 1-D series reference does not hold in 3-D, the interface nodes constrain the different lateral contraction of the two materials

xfail.reason: the SPD path solved a symmetric indefinite 6x6 block matrix without an error (relative residual 9.3e-17, solution correct to 2.2e-16): it does not detect that the matrix is not SPD
xfail.resolution: the returned solution is residual-checked, so the defect is an unverified structural claim, not a wrong answer; an opt-in SPD verification (inertia or pivot signs) is the follow-up; callers that need definiteness use solvers.diagnostics.inertia

xfail.reason: Preregistered time-convergence hypothesis (error falls by a factor >= 1.5 per doubling of the increments, err(200) <= err(25)/5) does not apply at the rate 1e-3 1/s: end-stress errors against the ODE are 1.9e-8, 3.7e-8, 3.7e-8, 1.5e-8 Pa for n = 25, 50, 100, 200 (1 ulp of 2.2e7 Pa), because after the yield transient the response is on the quasi-static steady state, which backward Euler integrates exactly. The production code agrees with the ODE to roundoff; the hypothesis is wrong for this rate. Rates 0.1 and 1 1/s pass the same check.
xfail.resolution: Kept as xfail(strict) with the measured values; a post hoc, clearly labelled check asserts agreement with the ODE to 1e-12 relative at this rate.

xfail.reason: Preregistered claim for n = 20, q_tr = 10 sigma_ref, dt = 1 s: q_new < 1e-3 q_tr. Measured q_new/q_tr = 0.1505 (q_new = 1.505e7 Pa). The production root agrees with an independent scipy brentq root of dt A (q/sigma_ref)^n = (q_tr - q)/(3G) to 1e-10, so the claim itself was wrong (creep stops relaxing where the rate balances the elastic unloading), not the code.
xfail.resolution: Hypothesis was wrong; kept as strict xfail. Replaced by the post hoc check test_c3g_post_hoc_high_stress_root_against_brentq (labelled post hoc) and the residual checks of C3f/C3g that passed.

xfail.reason: Preregistered global accuracy of the adaptive driver for the 1e-6..1e8 s relaxation with rtol = 1e-4: eps_cr relative error <= 1e-3 and |q - q_ref|/q0 <= 1e-3 at all 29 outputs. Measured max eps_cr relative error 2.10e-3 (t = 100 s) and max |q - q_ref|/q0 = 1.16e-3; 325 accepted steps (the step-count bound passed). Step doubling controls the local error only; the global error scales as ~0.2 sqrt(rtol) (2.1e-3, 6.7e-4, 2.1e-4 for rtol 1e-4, 1e-5, 1e-6).
xfail.resolution: Threshold not loosened; strict xfail. Post hoc characterisation test_c6a_post_hoc_global_error_decreases_with_rtol (error at rtol 1e-5 <= half the error at 1e-4) passes. The doc states that rtol is a local tolerance.

xfail.reason: Preregistered prediction that the nominal linearised std of the A_1000 amplitude (relaxation data only on 1e-3..1e-1 s, tau fixed at 0.1/10/1000 s, 1 % noise) is finite and exceeds the amplitude was wrong: the measured condition number of the design is 8.0e8 (the prereg only bounded it below by ~1e5), the smallest singular value falls below RANK_RTOL=1e-8 times the largest (rank 3 of 4), so the report returns std_nominal=None by design (as identification.identify does). The ambiguity is flagged (condition > 1e4, weakest combination 0.711*A_1000 - 0.703*equilibrium); only the numeric std is undefined. Post hoc and labelled: with rank_rtol=1e-12 the std/amplitude ratio is 3.5e6.
xfail.resolution: Kept as xfail(strict) with the measured values; the post hoc check test_D5a_post_hoc_std_with_a_stricter_rank_tolerance records the ratio under the stricter rank tolerance.

xfail.reason: worst case of the min-max design 1.21480e-4 vs 1.21135e-4 for the single t = 100 s design (+0.28 %); with a constant load the worst case is always the last time, so min-max reduces to J(100 s), and the bound formulation stopped (tol 1e-3, 95 iterations) at a worse local point than the direct run (134 iterations)
xfail.resolution: hypothesis too strong for a nonconvex problem with different iteration paths; a min-max study needs time-varying loads or several load cases, and a convergence test on the KKT residual rather than the step size
